text: ClinIQ takes clinical notes and H L 7 pathology results, and turns them into coded, validated FHIR, with a clinician always in the loop. Everything you are about to see is synthetic data.
A one-click sign-in as the shared demo clinician. Every view is written to an audit log.
This is the worklist: twenty Australian synthetic patients, held on a private FHIR R4 server in Sydney.
You can search by name, or by I H I.
On the chart, the banner repeats the patient's name, date of birth, sex and I H I, and allergies are always visible.
Decision support comes from a CDS Hooks service: e G F R by C K D E P I 2021, B M I, and care gaps.
The assistant answers common questions straight from the record, with no model involved, and every sentence is cited.
A citation opens the exact FHIR resource.
The drawer repeats the patient banner, so nothing is ever read against the wrong patient.
Requests for clinical advice are refused by a deterministic filter, before any model is called.
Pathology trends are grouped by analyte, with out-of-range results flagged, and units converted rather than merged by text.
Vitals follow, with blood pressure on one chart, and every chart has a table view.
The A U Patient Summary export is a FHIR document bundle, validated against A U P S 1.0, and it contains only confirmed data.
Now, notes to coded FHIR. Pick a note, then extract, code, validate and write.
A dry run first. Negated, family history and hypothetical mentions are never written, and each one shows why.
Now for real. With dry run switched off, the findings are written as unconfirmed Conditions, with Provenance.
The review queue highlights the excerpt in the note, repeats the patient banner, and shows the code with its confidence and rationale.
A clinician can confirm, change the code, or reject. Confirming records who verified it.
Back on the chart, the finding is now confirmed. Unconfirmed findings carry a badge, and are kept out of decision support.
H L 7 version 2 pathology comes in as an O R U message, is mapped to FHIR, validated, and answered with an acknowledgement.
On a dry run the acknowledgement says A A, and nothing is written. An unknown patient gets A E, and is never created.
The limits are stated plainly: synthetic data, an A I labelled evaluation, a free model behind the assistant, and the path to production.
ClinIQ. FHIR R4, A U Core, A U Patient Summary, H L 7 version 2, CDS Hooks, SMART on FHIR, and SNOMED CT A U. Built with Claude Code.
